title: You Could Learn to Pilot This ‘Flying Car’ in Just 5 Minutes
snippet: Is it a bird? Is it a plane? Is it a… flying Cybertruck? Nope, it’s a modular flying machine that will take to the skies next year.
fullText:
When I first laid eyes on the Aridge flying car at the IFA consumer electronics show in Berlin this past September, I didn’t fully understand what I was looking at.

Taking pride of place on the stand belonging to Chinese robotics company Xpeng, there was a van that bore more than a passing resemblance to a Cybertruck. It didn’t have any wings, and it looked far too dense to fly. Sitting next to it was a kind of oversized drone with a cabin just about large enough to fit two people. 

The two vehicles seemed like totally separate entities. It never would’ve occurred to me to assume they were two halves of one system – much less that the drone, with its substantial wingspan, could fold up to fit inside the van.

			

More from CNET

I now understand that this modular two-part flying car system is known formally as the Aridge Land Aircraft Carrier. The ground vehicle, also known as the mothership, is a chunky 5.5-meter-long van that can be driven with a standard license and fits in most parking spaces. It’s designed to store, carry and deploy the electric vertical takeoff and landing vehicle, or eVTOL, including its six foldable rotors, which can fly as high as a helicopter for 30km (about 19 miles).

This remarkable creation is the work of Deli Zhao, founder and president of Aridge, which is backed by robotics and auto company Xpeng. Speaking at Web Summit in Lisbon on Tuesday, Zhao presented himself as a man who was inspired to pursue a career building flying cars by Harry Potter and the Green Goblin, despite his lack of formal education.

“Dreams are very important,” Zhao said, as a video of him flying the eVTOL played on a screen in the background. Anyone can learn to fly the vehicle with just five minutes of training, he added. Or if you’re too tired to use the simple joystick, the eVTOL can fly itself autonomously.

“Everyone here can be a pilot,” Zhao said. “Everyone can be a captain.”

Flying ahead of the pack

This sounds like a story from the very kinds of science fiction that sparked the creation of the Land Aircraft Carrier in the first place – and yet, it isn’t. It’s far from the first time I’ve seen a flying car concept at a tech event. They’ve been showing up for almost a decade at this point. But what marks this one apart is that Xpeng says it has already taken 17,000 orders for the vehicle across China, the UAE and other Asian markets.

“Our advantage is we’re closer to commercialization,” Zhao said. Xpeng has established the world’s first mass-production factory for flying cars in Guangzhou, with trial production beginning in November last year. Right now, it’s ramping up capacity and improving quality with the aim of eventually being able to build a flying car in 30 minutes.

When I saw the eVTOL at IFA, it was so big that I struggled to fit it in one frame.

Aridge has worked through many different concepts, including flying motorcycles, to finally find one ready for commercial production (plus it has a six-seater air taxi and integrated flying car in the works for the future too). If you have $300,000 going spare, the Land Aircraft Carrier could soon be yours.

The vast majority of preorders are from individuals, according to Xpeng, but the vehicle has also been designed for use in tourism and search and rescue. Zhao said it solves multiple problems with existing eVTOLs simultaneously: storage (it lives in the back of the mothership), recharging (it charges as the mothership is driving), transportation to and from appropriate flight sites, and ease of use.

“I hope to make flying accessible to everyone as soon as possible,” Zhao said. Right now, it takes around 20 to 30 hours of training to acquire the sport pilot license you’d need to fly the eVTOL. In China, Zhao said he’s in conversation with the regulator to reduce this, emphasizing his vehicle’s ease of use.

A China-first product

Zhao said he’s learned a lot from the aviation sector in China, where the Land Aircraft Carrier has gone through extensive safety testing and will likely take to the skies first as a consumer-owned product as soon as next summer. Growing its low-altitude economy, which encompasses drone delivery and eVTOLs, is national policy for the country – in spite of calls for more regulation after a deadly crash in Beijing this summer.

Xpeng is also eyeing the European market, although the regulatory hurdles are likely to be substantial. “Europe’s aviation sector is highly developed,” Zhao said, expressing his respect for the region’s strict rules, but adding that the market was important. The company will also start exploring certification in the US next year, he said. Actual progress will depend on the outcomes, he added.

In spite of Zhao’s boundless optimism, it’s difficult to buy into the hype around his flying car without witnessing it in action in person. I’ve now seen the Land Aircraft Carrier twice in different locations and videos of it in operation, but I want to observe the eVTOL’s deployment from the mothership and its airborne skills for myself.

I still can’t fathom how the eVTOL fits in here.

At one point during his Web Summit talk, Zhao climbed into the cockpit of the eVTOL on stage. For a moment it seemed as though he might fly it right then and there inside Lisbon’s cavernous ME Arena. The audience raised their phones in unison, only to drop them again in disappointment when they realized Zhao wasn’t actually going to take off.

No matter how idiot-proof it might be to fly, it turns out European health and safety rules still apply.

Disclosure: Katie Collins traveled to Lisbon as a guest of Web Summit to serve as a panel moderator. Her reporting from the event was independent of that role.

title: Apple TV 4K review: The best streamer comes at a cost
snippet: It’s been four years since Apple last updated the Apple TV 4K, but a new version is here. There’s Siri AI support, a faster chip, an improved remote, and more. Here’s everything that’s changed, what’s better, and whether the new Apple TV 4K justifies its new $299 price. Pre-order the new Apple TV 4K Pre-order the new Siri Remote more…
fullText:
It’s been four years since Apple last updated the Apple TV 4K, but a new version is here. There’s Siri AI support, a faster chip, an improved remote, and more. 

Here’s everything that’s changed, what’s better, and whether the new Apple TV 4K justifies its new $299 price.

Pre-order the new Apple TV 4K

Pre-order the new Siri Remote

What’s changed

Performance

The Apple TV 4K’s overall design is largely unchanged. It’s still the same familiar black box that sits underneath your television. The only visual change is that the front status light has moved from the right side to the center. 

Inside, Apple has upgraded the A15 Bionic to the A19 chip, touting 50% faster CPU performance and twice the GPU performance.

Those are great improvements on paper. In practice, I’m not doing anything on my Apple TV that really stresses the performance. Compared to my third-generation Apple TV 4K, I’ve occasionally noticed slightly smoother animations and faster performance in apps that handle more processing locally, like Infuse.

I think the biggest advantage of the A19 chip is future-proofing. People tend to buy and keep these devices for years. In fact, I’m still using a first-generation Apple TV 4K from 2017 in my bedroom, and it still works just fine nearly a decade later. The A19 gives the new Apple TV plenty of performance headroom for future tvOS updates and more demanding apps, even if those advantages aren’t particularly noticeable today.

Siri Remote

The Siri Remote looks the same as before, but it now supports Precision Finding in the Find My app, making it easier to track down when misplaced. You can also play a sound on the remote to help locate it. I lose my Siri Remote all the time, so this honestly might be the change I’ve noticed and appreciated most in my 10 days testing the new Apple TV.

It’s worth noting Apple also sells the new Siri Remote separately for $59, and it’s compatible with every previous Apple TV 4K generation. You do, however, need a newer iPhone model to use Precision Finding.

Home Theater

One of the more interesting new features is support for a four-HomePod surround sound system. You need four HomePod (2nd generation) or HomePod mini 2 speakers, arranged in matching pairs at the front and rear of the room. Apple TV automatically calibrates the speakers based on their positions in the room.

For context, I typically use my Apple TV with a stereo pair of full-size HomePod (2nd generation) speakers. I’ve spent some time testing the new four-speaker surround sound setup by adding a pair of HomePod mini 2 speakers.

My house’s layout isn’t particularly well-suited for a traditional surround sound setup, but to my admittedly untrained ears, this sounds great. I can’t speak to how it compares to a dedicated surround sound system, but I appreciate Apple continuing to expand what’s possible with HomePods and Apple TV.

Siri AI

One of the biggest changes with the new Apple TV 4K is the addition of three far-field microphones. This means you can now interact with Siri without picking up the Siri Remote. In conjunction with this, Siri AI is also coming to Apple TV.

Siri AI brings the same broad world knowledge and personal-context capabilities you’ve experienced on iPhone and HomeView, but adapts them to finding and watching content on your television. Siri AI on Apple TV requires the owner of your Apple Home setup to have an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone or iPad.

Personal context requests also require a paired compatible device connected to the same Wi-Fi network as Apple TV.

A few things I’ve tried:

What movie did Zac recommend I watch?

What was that TV show Lily recommended a few weeks ago?

What are some baseball movies I might like? 

What did the vet say after Blake’s vet appointment? 

For each example, tvOS responded with a dedicated interface on Apple TV, showing the answer along with poster art, cast information, and more. It also offers built-in contextual suggestions when you ask for recommendations, so you can refine the results further.

You can also ask Siri contextual questions about the show or movie you’re watching. This includes things like “where was this show filmed?” and “when is the next season coming out?”

I’ve found Siri AI’s responses to those contextual questions less accurate. It struggles to accurately identify the show or movie that’s playing, leading to completely inaccurate responses to those types of questions.  

It’s worth noting that Siri AI is also coming to the second-generation Apple TV 4K from 2021 and the third-generation model from 2022. The far-field microphones are what’s exclusive to the new hardware. This lets you shout Siri commands into the air without talking directly into the Siri Remote. 

In my testing, hands-free Siri works relatively well, and it’s convenient to control Apple TV without reaching for the remote. It does a good job at picking up commands 

9to5Mac’s Take

I can’t go any further in this review without talking about the price. The Apple TV 4K (4th generation) costs $299. That’s a huge increase over previous Apple TV models. Here’s a brief history of Apple TV 4K pricing over the years to set the stage:

After Apple introduced the $129 Apple TV model in October 2022, I started to notice a change. More and more people had Apple TVs when I would visit. Friends and family who had previously bought an Amazon or Roku box, or just used their TV’s built-in software, had purchased an Apple TV.

At $299, I worry that type of adoption is going to come to a screeching halt. And it’s unfortunate because the Apple TV is so much better than anything else out there. tvOS is fast, clean, and relatively free of the clutter and advertisements you find on competing platforms. The Siri Remote is excellent, and the integration with the rest of Apple’s ecosystem is hard to beat.

I could justify the $299 price for the Apple TV 4K (4th generation) if it were just one option available in a broader lineup. If there were lower-priced options for people who don’t need all the bells and whistles. That’s not the case, though. In fact, this is the first Apple TV 4K generation to be sold in just one configuration. There’s no cheaper version with less storage or fewer features.

To Apple’s credit, these are devices that can last for years. The fact that I’m still using an Apple TV 4K from 2017 makes the $299 price a tiny bit easier to swallow, but it doesn’t really change my frustration.

Apple seems serious about its new smart home strategy. There’s the HomeView smart display, a new HomePod mini, and the Apple Home Collection family of smart home accessories launching later this year. One of the best ways to get deeper into people’s homes is by controlling how they watch TV. I can’t help but think pricing the Apple TV 4K out of reach for so many people will hinder those ambitions.

Don’t get me wrong, I love the Apple TV. I have three of them in my house. If one of them broke, I would reluctantly pay $299 for a new one. Whether you fall into that category is for you to decide. All I can say is that the new Apple TV 4K is the best streamer on the market.

title: Motorola MA2 wireless Android Auto adapter is now available, but at nearly twice the price
snippet: After first appearing months ago, the Motorola MA2 wireless Android Auto adapter is officially available for purchase in the US, but at a much higher price than expected. more…
fullText:
After first appearing months ago, the Motorola MA2 wireless Android Auto adapter is officially available for purchase in the US, but at a much higher price than expected.

Motorola MA2 at Amazon

While there’s a sea of wireless Android Auto adapters on the market today, the Motorola MA1 captured the attention of many as it was backed by Google directly. That was a double-edged sword, as we mentioned in our review, but it still got the job done. Now, it’s getting a sequel in MA2.

This new adapter was first announced way back in March 2026, bringing with it some welcome upgrades to the hardware including:

Physical on/off switch

Multipoint connectivity for pairing multiple phones

Button for switching paired phones, pairing mode

Modular USB-C/USB-A connection

You’ll also get both USB-C and USB-A cables in the box with the adapter, and it’s reiterated that the thing that makes this wireless Android Auto adapter stand out is that it’s the “only one engineered by Google.”

	

The new device is now available on Amazon for $69.99, and fills a gap as Motorola MA1 has been out of stock for months now. Where MA1 launched at nearly $100, MA2 is a much more reasonable price. That said, it’s not as cheap as we were expecting

Motorola MA2’s price was originally said to be $39.95, but the final price is $69.99 on Amazon. That price isn’t a complete surprise, as a listing on the Motorola Sound website has shown that price for months. Still, it’s a shame to see that the $40~ price promised won’t actually happen, and it’s equally frustrating that it effectively costs twice as much as it was said to.

As for shipping times, Motorola MA2 on Amazon is currently showing mid-late December delivery. That may vary based on your location and could end up being delivered early, too. It’s not uncommon for shipping timelines on new products to be incorrect for the first few days, and MA2 quite literally went on sale today as far as we can tell. That’s for the US, at least, as some users in other regions have been able to purchase the device for weeks, even months.

Are you picking up Motorola MA2? Our order is in, so stay tuned for hands-on coverage!

title: Foxconn revenue climbs 46%; Bloomberg forecasts 16M iPhone Duo sales
snippet: Key Apple manufacturing partner Foxconn has announced a year-on-year revenue increase of 46%, thanks to a mix of consumer electronics and server demand. Separately, Bloomberg Intelligence has forecast sales of 16 million iPhone Duo units in the first 12 months … more…
fullText:
Key Apple manufacturing partner Foxconn has announced a year-on-year revenue increase of 46%, thanks to a mix of consumer electronics and server demand.

Separately, Bloomberg Intelligence has forecast sales of 16 million iPhone Duo units in the first 12 months …

Foxconn is by far the largest contract manufacturer for iPhones, and at one point the majority of its revenue came from Apple. That hasn’t been true for some time, however, largely because of the company’s rapid expansion into servers for AI data centers and cloud storage.

All the same, some 29% of its revenue still comes from its consumer electronics division, of which Apple is by far the largest customer. It’s likely that at least some of its growth comes from the assembly of Apple products.

That’s backed by Bloomberg Intelligence prediction that sales of the iPhone Duo may hit 16 million units by September of next year. That would be well above earlier expectations, with Apple reportedly targeting 9.7M units in the first year before strong demand saw the company raise the goal to 14M.

Bloomberg says that with overall global smartphone demand decreasing due to a difficult economic environment, premium models like the Duo will become increasingly important to Apple’s revenue and profit.

title: Waze rolling out cyclist alerts based on real-time locations from Garmin trackers
snippet: Waze is officially rolling out alerts for cyclists along your route that leverages location data from Garmin trackers. more…
fullText:
Waze is officially rolling out alerts for cyclists along your route that leverages location data from Garmin trackers.

In an effort to “boost driver awareness” of nearby bicycle riders, Waze will start showing real-time alerts for nearby cyclists to drivers in the area. The feature shows both a location on the map ahead as well as a visible alert on screen.

Waze knows the location of a nearby cyclist through a partnership with Garmin, with “LiveTrack” location sharing from the Garmin Edge bike computer or Garmin smartwatches users to share location data with the Google-owned navigation app. 

Cyclists need to opt-in to the feature to have their location shown, and the alerts drivers see are temporary and anonymous. When cyclists end their ride, Waze alerts also go away.

	

Waze explains:

This feature is completely opt-in and built with privacy in mind. Drivers only see a temporary alert that a cyclist is nearby — never information about a specific cyclist or route. Plus, alerts automatically turn off the moment a cyclist ends their ride on their Garmin device.

This is rolling out starting today to the Waze apps on both Android and iOS.

title: Samsung bets that you’ll either buy a Galaxy S27 Pro or Ultra next year
snippet: Samsung is teeing up to kick off 2027 with an all-new lineup of flagship smartphones, and despite rising prices at your local Best Buy, the brand is still hedging that you’re going to pony up for the most premium model available. more…
fullText:
Samsung is teeing up to kick off 2027 with an all-new lineup of flagship smartphones, and despite rising prices at your local Best Buy, the brand is still hedging that you’re going to pony up for the most premium model available.

As reported by ETNews, Samsung is currently allotting over 70 percent of its total production capabilities to just the Galaxy S27 Ultra and the new Galaxy S27 “Pro” model expected to launch alongside it. That leaves the plain Galaxy S27 and the larger S27+ on the outside looking in. In comparison to this year’s launch, the Galaxy S26 Ultra made up about 50 percent of this series’ production volume, for a grand total of 18 million units.

	

In this case, Samsung isn’t actually betting next year’s S27 Ultra is going to surpass its predecessor by record numbers; rather, this is all about adding the S27 Pro as a fourth model for consumers to pick from. As the name implies, the S27 Pro will arrive packed with features usually kept for the Ultra tier exclusively, including Privacy Display and a matching design, but without an S Pen and with a smaller price. While Samsung plans to continue holding the Ultra tier at around 18 million units made, the S27 Pro will cut into the brand’s typical 35 million unit total by about 7 or 8 million. In other words, around 20 percent of sales that would’ve went to the regular S27 or S27+ are expected to move upmarket to this more expensive model.

Historical performance implies Samsung is probably correct here. While big displays are typically what consumers are drawn to, it does appear that the S27 Pro won’t be all that much smaller than the S27+. Considering the Pro should slot in right around the typical price point as the Plus model, it’s not hard to imagine plenty of would-be S27+ buyers moving to the Pro.

	

For what it’s worth, Samsung betting big on high-end devices usually pays off. We’re on year two of the Fold series seeing big successes — first with the redesigned Fold 7 in 2025, then with the reshaped Fold 8 this year — and the Galaxy S26 Ultra managed to become the best-selling Android phone in Q2 of this year in a list typically populated by iPhones and cheap Galaxy A-series models. Even with prices constantly on the rise, the people yearn for flagship smartphones. You just have to wonder where that ceiling actually is.

title: Jensen Huang didn’t show confidence in his successor, report says
snippet: Huang described Kress as a "deer in the headlights" during a meeting in summer.
fullText:
In Brief

Posted:

4:28 AM PST · November 13, 2026

Image Credits:Nvidia (opens in a new window)

		

							

											
									

					

	

Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang described Colette Kress, the company’s CFO who has now replaced him as interim CEO, as “a deer in the headlights” during a presentation earlier in the summer, the Wall Street Journal reported, citing an anonymous source.

Huang made the comment during a meeting with Nvidia’s finance team about the company’s plans to provide guarantees worth billions of dollars to data center operators that couldn’t afford to buy its chips up front, according to the report.

He reportedly also said Kress was a person who couldn’t help him steer strategy or decision-making.

Kress has been with Nvidia for over 13 years now, after serving as SVP and CFO of Cisco’s Business Technology and Operations Finance. The report said she has questioned Nvidia’s program-focused, credit-based deals involving Huang’s son-in-law Nico Caprez, and wanted to know how to decide which deals are beneficial, how to value guarantees, and determine returns.

Earlier in the year, she had scaled back on Nvidia’s commitment for OpenAI’s ambitious Ohio data center project. The company was in talks to provide $250 billion in credit to OpenAI but ended up committing $105 billion.

Huang resigned Thursday after reports of two extramarital affairs, including one with the company’s VP for healthcare, Kimberly Powell. The company is also investigating a possible Chinese espionage plot.

After Huang’s resignation, Reuters reported that he was having a third affair with another employee. Nvidia is currently searching for a permanent CEO to replace Huang, who had the top job for over 33 years.

title: You can now set up Gemini’s Google Wallet integration for ‘personal finance insights’
snippet: As we spotted in September, the Gemini app is adding Google Wallet integration in the US that makes possible “responses informed by your spending habits.” more…
fullText:
As we spotted in September, the Gemini app is adding Google Wallet integration in the US that makes possible “responses informed by your spending habits.”

In the Gemini app, @Google Wallet allows you to: 

Visualize spending: Questions like “can we review my spending from last quarter so I can save $1,000 over the next three months?” enable Gemini to generate dynamic charts tracking cash flow, asset allocation, and budgets directly in your chat.

Find forgotten subscriptions: If you ask “what subscriptions am I still paying for, and did any of them go up in price this year?” Gemini finds recurring charges across your linked accounts and flags price increases.

Budget for the holidays: When you ask “how much did I spend on gifts and travel last year? Use that to help me set a holiday budget for this year,” Gemini will look at your transactions from the last year and suggest a budget tailored to you.

The interactive visualizations (seen above) are quite cool. This integration leverages third-party service Plaid to “securely link your financial accounts from your credit cards and banks” to Google Wallet.

On the privacy front, this integration is read-only, with Gemini not able to “move, manage, or invest your money.”

	

You decide if and when you want to opt in to this experience, and you can turn the connection on or off at any time. Learn more here.

Once enabled, @Google Wallet is available in the Gemini app on Android, iOS, and web for US users. To get started, go to Customize > Connectors or gemini.google.com/customize/connectors.

Google bills this as an expansion of Personal Intelligence, which already taps into Gmail, Photos, Search, and YouTube to customize responses. The company today also highlighted the launch of Memory Summary from earlier this week.

title: Reddit Reviews goes against the whole philosophy of the platform, say users
snippet: Many Redditors have expressed dismay at the launch of Reddit Reviews, a new AI-powered feature which aims to summarise posts about particular products. Reddit is positioning the feature as a way to save time and effort when researching a potential purchase, but many Redditors say that replacing human interaction with AI summaries is antithetical to the whole philosophy of the platform – and is going to make the existing spam problem massively worse … more…
fullText:
Many Redditors have expressed dismay at the launch of Reddit Reviews, a new AI-powered feature which aims to summarise posts about particular products.

Reddit is positioning the feature as a way to save time and effort when researching a potential purchase, but many Redditors say that replacing human interaction with AI summaries is antithetical to the whole philosophy of the platform – and is going to make the existing spam problem massively worse …

The value of customer reviews on ecommerce platforms like Amazon is becoming increasingly questionable thanks to practices like astroturfing by brands and offering people free products in return for five-star reviews.

That’s led to Reddit becoming one of the most trusted sources of feedback and advice on potential purchases, precisely because it’s a forum in which real people are free to express their true opinions. Indeed, many use a filter in their Google searches to draw content from Reddit specifically, adding the suffix ‘site:reddit.com’.

	

Reddit certainly isn’t immune to astroturfing – that is, fake posts by brands posing as ordinary users – but moderators put a lot of work into deleting spam and other inauthentic posts.

Reddit Reviews

The platform yesterday announced the launch of Reddit Reviews, in which AI summarises the posts made about particular products and product categories. It’s being pitched as a way for people to save time when seeking the product opinions of Redditors.

Across Reddit’s communities, people discuss everything from hobbies and daily life to products they’re researching. By offering perspectives grounded in real experience, these conversations provide valuable context in every purchase decision journey […]

Today, we are starting to test Reddit Reviews, a new experience that organizes product conversations from across Reddit into dedicated reviews and highlights the most important takeaways from across our communities.

Redditor and mod backlash

However, as CNET spotted, the move has led to a backlash by many Redditors and subreddit moderators.

“I’ve already seen this in practice and it is a nightmare. It turns a basic conversation into an ad-ridden distracting mess. It’s horrible to read and had me fleeing every thread I saw it in.”

“I am a moderator on a couple of health subs and we explicitly do not allow advertisements because most of them are bullshit slop and completely predatory for vulnerable and newly diagnosed patients. We do not want, or need this, on our subs!”

“The enshittification continues.”

“Yeah, this definitely isn’t going to lead to even more fake account stealth marketing efforts across the site.”

“This is going to make our spam fighting even worse. This is horrible.”

“Every decision made by Reddit lately encourages spam and/or abuse that will make spam.”

“Not a single person who uses Reddit wants this.”

“You are incentivising existing spammers to continue or step up their activities, now that there’s a new well they can poison.”

9to5Mac’s Take

I find it hard to disagree with the view that almost every monetization step the platform has made has degraded the user experience. This seems almost guaranteed to be another one.

title: Amazon’s new Ring cameras are mounted to roving robots, including $250 Drone Cam
snippet: Amazon’s Ring brand is today launching a new “Robotics” division that will start with two offerings – a $250 Ring Drone Cam and a $1,000 Rover Cam. more…
fullText:
Amazon’s Ring brand is today launching a new “Robotics” division that will start with two offerings – a $250 Ring Drone Cam and a $1,000 Rover Cam.

Indoor cameras can be invaluable for securing your home, but also just in keeping an eye on what’s going on when you’re not home. To that end, Ring has been working on cameras that can be sent around the home remotely, and they’re finally launching early next year.

Ring first showed off its Drone Cam in 2020, but never actually brought the product to market. That changes in January of next year, when the Ring Drone Cam will be available for $249.99. The camera, Amazon expains, is “a flying indoor security camera that goes where you need it, when you need it, and stays docked and out of sight when you don’t.” You can set flight routes on a schedule, have the drone automatically investigate tripped sensors in your Ring system, and more. The camera is only active when the drone is in flight, and it’s emphasized that the drone is not “quiet,” it’s “meant to be seen and heard.”

The other robot Amazon’s Ring is launching is the Rover Cam, which is built on the back of Amazon Astro. It has a telescoping camera and rolls around your home on “scheduled patrols” as well as being able to automatically investigate tripped sensors. It also features two-way audio and a built-in siren to deter intruders from an area, while also features continuous 4K recording. 

	

Ring is mainly pitching this one for businesses, and it costs $999.99 with pre-orders open now ahead of a December 16 release date.

snippet: Screens, the remote desktop app for iPhone, iPad, Mac, and Apple Vision Pro, is adding two highly-requested features. Version 5.10 introduces remote Mac audio and automatic desktop resizing through Apple’s High Performance Screen Sharing technology. more…
fullText:
Screens, the remote desktop app for iPhone, iPad, Mac, and Apple Vision Pro, is adding two highly-requested features. Version 5.10 introduces remote Mac audio and automatic desktop resizing through Apple’s High Performance Screen Sharing technology.

Screens adds remote Mac audio, automatic resizing, and High Performance Screen Sharing

The remote desktop can now adjust to your screen when you rotate your iPhone or iPad, change your multitasking layout, or resize a connection window on Mac and Vision Pro. You can also choose a fixed resolution.

Remote audio lets you hear sound from a compatible Mac, while HEVC streaming promises smoother video, scrolling, and animations.

Edovia says a fast, stable connection with low latency is required. Screens can fall back to standard screen updates when network conditions deteriorate while preserving features like resizing and display privacy.

The update also introduces a Metal-based renderer designed to improve performance across connections, including Windows, Linux, and Raspberry Pi.

Other changes include a Liquid Glass connection carousel and floating toolbar improvements on iPhone and iPad.

Edovia’s announcement has the full rundown. Screens 5.10 is available on the App Store as a free download with in-app purchases. Subscriptions start at $4.99/month or $29.99/year, with a $199.99 lifetime option also available.

NXTPAPER technology is designed to be easy on your eyes, with flicker-free dimming and a special textured matte layer that keeps glare down and visibility high. 

	

TCL often sells this as an e-reader alternative since the phone has “NXTPAPER modes” that alter the screen’s color for a gentler reading experience. Device Connectivity

title: Google Gemini rolling out ‘Memory summary’ with everything it remembers about you
snippet: Google Gemini now offers a “Memory summary” to “view, edit, and delete what Gemini Apps understands about you.” more…
fullText:
Google Gemini now offers a “Memory summary” to “view, edit, and delete what Gemini Apps understands about you.”

On the web, you can access this new experience from Settings > Personal Intelligence (or gemini.google.com/personalization-settings).

This loads a list with categories like: The Essentials (“snapshot of your core background, location, and key relationships”), Career & Professional Projects, Travel & Daily Gear, Media & Entertainment, and Fitness & Lifestyle. Each has several bullet points with specific details.

The text field at the bottom lets you “Add or remove details.” For example:

	

To add info: “Add to my memory that I speak Japanese.”

To remove info: “Remove my old phone number from your memory.”

Google says “Gemini may ask follow-up questions if your request is ambiguous to ensure your summary remains accurate.”

The pencil icon in the top-right corner lets you make broader edits. In the three-dot overflow menu, you’ll find “Memory history” to see “when specific information was added or modified.”

Officially, this feature is available for Google AI subscribers in US English with Keep Activity and Memory enabled. We’re not seeing this rolled out on Android or iOS yet, but the experience should be similar.

title: Binance warns iPhone crypto holders of security flaw researchers say remains unpatched
snippet: Crypto exchange Binance has warned iPhone users about an iOS vulnerability that could allow malicious apps to access sensitive data stored by other apps. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Crypto exchange Binance has warned iPhone users about an iOS vulnerability that could allow malicious apps to access sensitive data stored by other apps. Here are the details.

Researchers say flaw remains unpatched

In a post published on X (via AppleInsider), Binance says that a vulnerability called worse_query could allow “malicious apps to read local files from other apps, putting seed phrases, private keys, and login credentials at risk across the entire ecosystem.”

Binance says the flaw affects iOS 26.7.1, iOS 27.0.1, and iOS 27.2. However, a Community Note points out that researchers describe the vulnerability as an unpatched zero-day and that Apple’s latest security updates, including iOS 27.2.1 (the current version at the time of writing), do not mention a fix.

A vulnerability (worse_query) affecting iOS 26.7.1, 27.0.1, and 27.2 allows malicious apps to read local files from other apps, putting seed phrases, private keys, and login credentials at risk across the entire ecosystem. This is an iOS-level issue, not unique to Binance.…

— Binance (@binance) November 10, 2026

That said, in addition to updating their devices, Binance recommends that iPhone crypto holders take the following immediate actions:

Delete any apps installed from untrusted sources (such as sideloaded or manually signed IPAs).

Update iOS and all apps to the latest official versions.

If you suspect a breach, transfer funds to a new wallet created on a clean device and reset all active login sessions.

The vulnerability was disclosed by security researchers @0xjohnny and @forcequitOS, who published a proof of concept on GitHub demonstrating how it can be used to bypass iOS sandbox protections, which normally prevent apps from accessing each other’s files.

Researcher @forcequitOS also noted that neither iOS 27.2.1 nor iOS 27.3 beta 1 patches the vulnerability.

Just as a general statement so there isn’t any confusion about it, worse_query is *not* patched in iOS 27.2.1 and 27.3 beta 1. I’ll update version support on the readme when it’s patched.

— forcequit (@forcequitOS) November 10, 2026

Although the researcher describes the code as intended for developers and not useful on its own, other developers have already built apps using it, including a file manager that can access, modify, and delete data belonging to other apps without requiring a jailbreak.

According to The Hacker News, neither Binance nor the researchers have reported any attacks or cryptocurrency thefts involving the vulnerability so far.

title: iOS 27.2 has two CarPlay improvements, here’s what’s new
snippet: iOS 27.2 arrived last month with new features for Messages, Apple TV, and more, plus two improvements for CarPlay. Here’s what’s new for CarPlay users. more…
fullText:
iOS 27.2 arrived last month with new features for Messages, Apple TV, and more, plus two improvements for CarPlay. Here’s what’s new for CarPlay users.

#1: Apple Podcasts adds sections for New Episodes and Continue Playing

Apple Podcasts in iOS 27.2 adds two new sections to the Home tab: ‘New Episodes’ and ‘Continue Playing.’

Essentially, Apple has rethought how the core ‘Up Next’ queue of its Podcasts app works.

Like you would expect, ‘New Episodes’ contains only the latest episodes from your favorite shows. But after you’ve started an episode, you’ll find it in the ‘Continue Playing’ row just below.

This overhaul to podcast management makes it easier to find the latest episodes of your shows and also pick up where you previously left off. I’m a big fan of the change.

#2: Siri AI upgrades

Siri AI introduces a variety of upgrades in iOS 27.2, including two that carry over to CarPlay as well.

Per Apple’s release notes:

Siri AI can recall your past conversations, so you can ask Siri about something it told you before, like the restaurants it recommended last week

Siri AI can draw from more sources to give you a great answer, including photos attached in Messages, Calendar event attendees, your voicemails, and better results from Safari history and Reading List

It can take some adjustment to remember that Siri AI is available in the car just like on iPhone. But CarPlay is an especially useful platform for Apple’s more powerful assistant.

Bonus: Apple Music’s new app icon and design tweaks

It’s arguable whether this qualifies as an “improvement,” but it is a change worth mentioning. iOS 27.2 includes a new app icon for Apple Music, plus some minor design tweaks in the app.

These changes are related to the broader rebrand of Apple Music that was recently unveiled.

title: Google Fi brings back network switching with ‘secondary’ partner, expands W+ beyond Pixel
snippet: Google Fi Wireless is rolling out a big update today with the return of network switching thanks to a “secondary” partner. more…
fullText:
Google Fi Wireless is rolling out a big update today with the return of network switching thanks to a “secondary” partner.

At the beginning, Project Fi was known for giving subscribers access to both T-Mobile and Sprint networks. Over time, the second partner went away, leaving one predominant network.

Google Fi is now bringing back a second partner as part of its new “super network.” Most users will be on the “Primary network,” but Google Fi will automatically switch users to the “Secondary network” if it meaningfully improves performance with so-called “smart thresholds” for doing so. At launch, there is no manual switching.

Google is not naming the second network today, but did share that Ultra Wideband is supported. Officially, you are switching between “two of America’s fastest 5G networks.”

	

Fi Wireless does note that users have top priority, so data is never deprioritized on the Primary network. Meanwhile, there’s “highest QCI priority” on the backup network that means subscribers are among the last to be slowed down when there’s congestion. This is also available internationally when local partner networks are available with the Flexible and Unlimited Premium plans.

Network switching will first be supported on Pixel 9 and newer devices that have a Google Fi eSIM (and no other SIM active). It makes use of Android’s Multiple Enabled Profiles (MEP) eSIM technology that allows for two carrier profiles on a single chip.

	

The Google Fi app gains a “Your super network” card in the Home tab that shows whether you’re connected to the Primary or Secondary network. “See activity” lets you view switching history and when it last occurred. Google will also note if you’re in range of W+ networks.

Google today is also expanding its Wi-Fi Auto Connect+ network beyond Pixel phones to select Samsung Galaxy (S23, Fold/Flip 5, and newer) and modern Motorola phones. These premium Wi-Fi networks are available in millions of airports, malls, stores, and restaurants. The connection happens automatically, with the Google Fi Virtual Carrier Network encrypting data. 

The final update today sees the companion app gain “Ask Fi.” This AI-powered chat is meant to quickly provide answers and guided troubleshooting for common issues. You can request human support with seamless handoff that keeps the chat context.

These Google Fi updates start rolling out today, with network switching seeing gradual availability. This launch is accompanied by several deals:

“For new subscribers, get $500 off instantly and $599 back over 24 monthly credits when you purchase the new Google Pixel 11 Pro, plus $10/mo service credit for 2 years with the Unlimited Premium plan. Ends 11/18/26.”

“Already have a Pixel but not using Google Fi? Get 50% off select unlimited plans for 12 months. Ends 12/1/26.”

title: Google Home update fixes Nest ‘Live View’ issues, improves Nest Hub and Gemini for speakers
snippet: A new Google Home update is rolling out with a fix for “Live View” issues affecting Nest Cam devices, improvements for the Nest Hub, upgrades for Gemini, and more. more…
fullText:
A new Google Home update is rolling out with a fix for “Live View” issues affecting Nest Cam devices, improvements for the Nest Hub, upgrades for Gemini, and more.

As per usual, the latest Google Home update can be split up into a few categories, starting with Gemini. Still in early access, enrolled users can expect further improvements to smart home controls, faster timers, and “more conversational voice feedback,” as well as faster Broadcasts.

Most notable on the Gemini front is improvements to Nest Hubs, with smart displays now showing “relevant images when helpful” when you ask questions.

Visual answers with images on smart displays: On-screen answers on smart displays now will include relevant images when helpful so you can take in information at a glance.

In the Google Home app, Google is adding a “Google Home Premium” page to the settings menu, an “Eco Mode Everywhere” toggle for homes with multiple Nest Thermostats, and support for Home keys in Google Wallet for compatible locks.

	

Google Wallet rolling out digital Google Home keys with supported locks on Android

More software updates are rolling out for older Nest Cam devices, including a fix for the “Live View” issue that’s been in place on some devices such as Nest Hello. You can also remove an unmigrated Nest Hello from the Home app even if it is offline. Other camera updates in this update include:

More reliable camera history player controls (Android): Fixed issues in camera event history where the previous and next event buttons or player controls could be missing or unresponsive on still-image events, timeline gaps, or playback error screens, or get stuck loading when rotating your phone.

Fewer unnecessary Nest account linking prompts (Android): Fixed an issue where already-linked users could be prompted with “Do you have a Nest account?” during brief network interruptions.

Clearer account relinking for partner cameras (Android): Fixed an issue where third-party cameras with an expired partner account link appeared offline instead of showing the option to relink your account.

Offline legacy Nest Doorbell removal (Android): Restored the option in device settings to remove an offline unmigrated Nest Doorbell (wired, 1st gen).

Software updates for Nest Cam Indoor (1st gen), Nest Cam Outdoor (1st gen), Nest Doorbell (wired, 1st gen / Nest Hello), Nest Cam IQ Indoor, and Nest Cam IQ Outdoor migrated to the Google Home app:

Fixed live streaming connection issues on certain network connections: Resolved an issue where live streaming could fail to connect over certain internet connections (such as PPPoE, fiber, or mobile hotspots) while event history continued recording normally, and improved live stream responsiveness and smoothness.

Restored event thumbnails on Nest Cam IQ: Fixed an issue on Nest Cam IQ Indoor and Nest Cam IQ Outdoor where event previews in the Google Home app could appear blank.

Improved playback timestamps and camera reliability: Improved camera clock accuracy for reliable event history timestamps, updated security certificates, and fixed stability issues to reduce unexpected camera restarts.

On the AI agent front, Google Home MCP connections now allow agents to control automations as well as accessing new controls and status checks across “thermostats, fans, air purifiers, robot vacuums, lighting effects, kitchen appliances, EV chargers, and smoke and carbon monoxide alarms.”

Google is also rolling out smart speaker updates right now, but details on what’s new are limited.

title: Apple TV launches new sign language accessibility feature
snippet: Apple today launched a neat new accessibility feature for the Apple TV streaming service. Users will now have the option to watch with a sign language interpretation for some of Apple’s original movies. The feature is launching this Friday with the debut of the new film Being Heumann, as well as F1: The Movie. Support for more titles will follow later. more…
fullText:
Apple today launched a neat new accessibility feature for the Apple TV streaming service. Users will now have the option to watch with a sign language interpretation for some of Apple’s original movies. 

The feature is launching this Friday with the debut of the new film Being Heumann, as well as F1: The Movie. Support for more titles will follow later.

Alongside those two films, Apple said that sign language options will be available for Greyhound and Way of the Warrior Kid later this year, with more to come.

To access the new functionality, you need to be using the Apple TV app on iPhone, iPad or Mac running 27.2 or later. The feature will also be available on some versions of the Apple TV app on other platforms. 

By default, the Sign Language controls are hidden. If you want to use the feature, firstly go to the Settings app -> TV app, and enable the Sign Language display. 

Then, on eligible titles, a new Sign Language button will appear in the player controls. You can simply toggle to enable, and choose from American Sign Language or British Sign Language modes. 

When enabled, a signing interpreter then appears in the corner of the frame, synced with the video playback. 

When browsing the catalog, sign language availability will also be shown next to the usual subtitle and audio language information. Users will also be able to search “with ASL” or “with BSL” to find compatible titles.

snippet: Last week CNET published an extensive battery test and the iPhone came out on top. But it wasn’t just one iPhone model that performed well, as several iPhones topped CNET’s list. more…
fullText:
Last week CNET published an extensive battery test and the iPhone came out on top. But it wasn’t just one iPhone model that performed well, as several iPhones topped CNET’s list.

iPhone 18 Pro Max has best battery performance per CNET test, with iPhone 17 and iPhone 18 Pro winners too

CNET pitted 32 modern smartphones against each other to see how battery life compared.

The winner? iPhone 18 Pro Max, which was followed closely by two other iPhone models.

Here’s the top 10 list, which contains several ties:

As you can see, iPhone 17 and iPhone 18 Pro both tied for second place alongside a pair of Android models. iPhone 18 Pro Max was the sole model that beat every other.

Each battery test is going to be a bit different, so results may vary depending on how you stress-test a phone. That said, here’s the method behind CNET’s test:

Each phone was put through a 3-hour streaming video test and a 45-minute anecdotal stress test, both with the battery at 100%. The results show the remaining battery percentage – the higher, the better. We averaged the results to determine our rankings

CNET says that in the 45-minute stress test they “stream videos, make a video call, play games and scroll social media.” So it’s an attempt at replicating normal use.

fullText:
Android tablets have always been a bit of a touchy subject, but it’s abundantly clear that the form factor is making a comeback. But, as someone who’s a fan of the smaller sizes, are you actually using the gargantuan Android tablets that every company seems obsessed with? In other words – are you the customer for the Android tablets these brands are selling?

9to5Google Weekender by Ben Schoon is a part of our free newsletter that also includes ‘Inbox,’ a twice-weekly roundup of key stories from around the web by Daniel Bader. Sign up here to get Weekender delivered to your inbox every Sunday along with ‘Inbox’ on Tuesday and Thursday. You can find past issues here.

Sign up below to access the web version.

For a while there, Android tablets had hit what felt like a dead end. Bigger smartphones and cooling of the tablet market as a whole, along with the general sentiment that Apple was doing a way better job with the iPad anyway, left the category in a place that felt stagnant – and that’s the nice way of putting it. 

	

But, over the past few years, Android tablets have had a renaissance. 

New form factors, big releases from a variety of brands, and flagship-tier devices left and right. Despite Android’s push into foldables and still-huge displays on nearly every smartphone, tablets are very much back. Prior to RAMageddon’s worst impacts, tablet sales were growing for nearly everyone, and Android brands were seeing a larger slice of the pie.

Anyway, this is on my mind right now because I’ve had a lot of Android tablets arrive in my office in the past few weeks, capping off a lot of tablet announcements in the past few months. I just finished up with Redmagic Astra 2, a tablet I think fits the description of “Android’s iPad Mini OLED,” and I’m in the process of moving into tablets from Lenovo and Amazon. Our Jordan Floyd has also been testing out the Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra behind the scenes. And if there’s one trend amongst recent tablet releases, it’s that big tablets seem to be the primary focus among a lot of brands.

Take Amazon’s new Google Play-equipped Alexa Tablet lineup, for example.

The Alexa Tablet 12 is the crown jewel of the lineup, packing the most powerful specs and a premium anti-glare display. It’s the only one that gets a “Pro” moniker, while the 11-inch and 8-inch models are noticeable steps down. Unboxing the Alexa Tablet 8 this week, for example, I was immediately reminded this is not a premium device – the screen makes that clear without any hesitation whatsoever. It was a case of whiplash after setting up the Lenovo Yoga Tab Plus Gen 2 with its 4K display.

Amazon Alexa Tablet 8

It’s a weird one for me. I’ve never been a big fan of these super-sized Android tablets (or iPads, for that matter). I can get behind a 10-inch or 11-inch model, but I find myself more at home on the smaller slates. They’re fantastic for travel as an alternative to draining my phone’s battery, while I find myself just reaching for a laptop instead if I want a bigger screen. A big tablet, regardless of specs, can rarely replace a proper laptop for me, so lugging both around just sounds like more trouble than it’s worth.

But, clearly, people are buying these bigger slates. Samsung appears to be seeing enough success with its mammoth Galaxy Tab S Ultra lineup to keep the 14.6-inch tablet around each year while the smaller sizes are now on an every-other-year cycle. Lenovo’s lineup is virtually all underpowered when the screen size goes down, aside from the Legion Tab that’s now $900. 

Lenovo Yoga Tab Plus Gen 2

Are you buying these bigger tablets? What are you using them for?

I imagine that most folks opting for a bigger tablet are using these in the place of a laptop. Thinner and lighter, longer battery life, etc. And in cases like the Alexa Tablet 12 Pro and its $550~ price tag, I get the appeal. Lenovo Yoga Tab Plus Gen 2 takes that down a notch for me at $799 – you’re getting into laptop territory there – but it still is a compelling-enough alternative if it fits your needs. The Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra at $1,400 plus a $200 keyboard, yeah I don’t get that one at all. 

Let’s discuss! I want to know if you’re using an Android tablet, what you’re using it for, and what size you actually prefer.

title: Google’s latest Search upgrade promises better answers to your most complicated questions
snippet: Powered by Gemini 4 Hydrogen, Google's AI Mode is getting better at understanding complex queries, surfacing relevant links, and delivering richer visual responses.
fullText:
Google Search is getting better at understanding complicated questions, including those with multiple parts, highly specific requests, or confusing typos. The updates are coming via the company’s newly released Gemini 4 Hydrogen model, which Google claims is its “biggest model improvement to Search yet.”

While Google’s frontier models, Gemini 4 Carbon and Gemini 4 Argon, are best at deep reasoning for hard problems, Hydrogen is designed for fast execution across a variety of agentic workflows, or tasks in which an AI carries out multiple steps on its own, the company explained in an announcement.

The idea behind the model’s release is that using the most powerful model isn’t always needed — sometimes a faster, cheaper, and reasonably smart one will do. Google says Hydrogen completes tasks 2.5 times faster than Gemini 3.8 Flash, its previous fast model, but it’s still pretty smart, even beating the more powerful Gemini 4 Argon on one broad intelligence benchmark, the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, at its default high thinking level.

In Search, Hydrogen brings several improvements, including a better understanding of user intent, the ability to offer more helpful links and visual responses, and better answers across the different languages supported by Google’s AI Mode.

In terms of intent, Google says Hydrogen can handle more nuanced and complicated questions more quickly. This means people can ask their questions in their natural train of thought, including those that have multiple parts or that include highly specific requests. Hydrogen is also better at navigating hard-to-understand typos, Google says. Because of its improvements and better ability to follow instructions and call the right tools, Hydrogen is able to more precisely address each part of a user’s question. 

Its advanced reasoning also improves Search’s fan-out technique, which breaks down a single user’s prompt into multiple subqueries. This allows people to discover websites related to the query that they may have otherwise missed, the blog post explains. 

The addition of Hydrogen to Search will also mean more images, structured responses, comparison tables, and custom tools will appear as visual responses to users’ queries in AI Mode.  

Image Credits:Google
Image Credits:Google
Image Credits:Google
Image Credits:Google

Google also says Hydrogen can work on its own for everyday work in areas like writing code, running tests, or verifying code changes, or it can be paired with Carbon and Argon in workflows that combine several models.

The model offers four thinking levels: low, medium, high (default), and a new, extra-high tier (“xhigh”), all of which are designed to complete tasks faster with fewer output tokens.

On multi-step tasks like deep research, data analysis, and broad codebase navigation, Hydrogen ranks No. 5 on Agent Arena’s benchmarks, the company pointed out. 

In addition to Search, Gemini 4 Hydrogen is coming to all tiers of Google’s AI Studio, the Gemini API, the Gemini App, and the paid AI Pro and Ultra subscribers in Google’s Antigravity development platform.

Google says the Hydrogen update is rolling out to all Search users globally.

title: After Jensen Huang, Big Tech Has a Chance to Learn From Nvidia’s Mistakes
snippet: Tech insiders and commentators say Nvidia will survive Huang’s departure, but it’s time for more accountability among CEOs.
fullText:
What now for Nvidia? This was the question on everyone’s lips at the illustrious Web Summit technology conference in Lisbon on Thursday in the hours after CEO Jensen Huang announced his resignation.

Huang’s departure followed a series of allegations that he had multiple extramarital affairs, including one with an Nvidia employee and one with a woman who has been identified as a possible Chinese spy. The company, whose computer chips are at the core of generative AI’s disruptive powers, is valued at around $4 trillion, making it one of the most valuable in the world. A co-founder, Huang has been with Nvidia since its earliest days three decades ago, making it hard to imagine the company without him at the helm.

There’s nothing quite like a salacious, market-moving scandal to create a buzz at a tech event. The Web Summit organizers leaned into the news, quickly assembling a panel of tech experts to discuss whether Nvidia was bigger than its CEO.

			

More from CNET

Nothing in the allegations changes the fact that Huang is probably the godfather of the AI revolution, said investor and financial writer Adam Kobeissi. “He was the central figure,” Kobeissi said, even if he wasn’t the only person responsible for Nvidia’s success.

“This company is going to survive and thrive with or without him,” he added. “I don’t think this is some sort of bubble-popping moment where everything comes crumbling down.”

Sweeping financial investments and expectations across the AI industry have driven stock prices and company valuations to dizzying heights, with many critics warning of a bubble just waiting to burst with destabilizing effects. As powerful as Nvidia has become, it could be caught in the center of such a maelstrom. 

While such a concentration of power is not the way to create resilient companies, said Ryan LaSalle, CEO of cybersecurity company Nisos, like Kobeissi he thinks Nvidia will weather the storm. 

Interim Nvidia CEO Collette Kress, who has been with the company since 2013, is known for having a ton of loyalty within Nvidia, he said. “In a company of that much brainpower, there will be some natural leaders who can help shepherd them to the next chapter.”

Great power and no responsibility

One big question put to panel participants was whether Nvidia’s board made a mistake allowing one person to have so much power. 

It wasn’t just a mistake of corporate culture, said Carissa Veliz, associate professor of philosophy at the Oxford Institute for Ethics in AI. It was also a mistake in terms of democracy.

For one person to wield so much power over decisions affecting the economy and national security means something has gone wrong and has revealed how vulnerable we are, Veliz said. If we look at the history of corporations, she said, there used to be a tradition of proving to the government that you were doing good for your country to earn your right to exist and get certain tax breaks.

“At the moment, we have shifted from that kind of framework to a framework in which a corporation is allowed to be essentially a kind of psychopath that only cares about its own profits, that only has duties to shareholders and which can be structured in any way, including a very powerful CEO with very little oversight,” she said.

Gil Duran, author of The Nerd Reich: Silicon Valley Fascism and the War on Democracy, said that he thought Nvidia’s errors in the lead-up to this moment would be studied in business and public relations crisis management classes.

“The board was completely missing out on most of the truth and the facts,” he said, referencing news reports that said Huang a year ago hired a law firm known for covering up sex scandals and President Donald Trump in May had been told about the CEO’s affair with the alleged Chinese spy.

“I don’t think there’s any other way to look at it but a catastrophe,” he said. 

An end to the era of ‘small king’ CEOs?

Duran and Veliz agreed that it was time to ensure tech CEOs face real oversight.

“These guys face no accountability and no supervision, and that’s part of the problem,” said Veliz. “These kind of small kings have their own small kingdoms… and they get away with almost anything.”

CEOs like Elon Musk at SpaceX and Sam Altman at OpenAI have enormous influence not only in their own companies but also across the national economy.

What we’re seeing in Huang’s downfall is the shattering of a myth about genius founders, said Duran. He questioned whether it would spark actual change, however, given that the market’s addiction to the narrative of great, powerful founders.

“The fact that they can just tumble markets with their personal lives that become geopolitical crises – this is an insane amount of power to outsource,” he said. 

If we can tone down the myth, this moment provides a chance to look at where we’ve gone wrong and do better, Veliz said. There’s opportunity here, she added – to raise up companies that can build the kinds of technology we need, support democracies rather than erode them, aren’t based on surveillance and prediction, and can behave transparently.

Lessons from a scandal

For every other tech behemoth out there, there is plenty to be learned from Huang’s downfall. The concentration of power in one individual is not, as LaSalle pointed out, a safe long-term strategy.

What’s needed is more oversight and accountability from a company’s board of directors. In announcing Huang’s resignation, Nvidia also said it was appointing its first chairman for its board.

Huang’s entanglement with a potential honeypot is also an opportunity for tech companies to think about security, said LaSalle. No matter how sophisticated cybersecurity threats are becoming in the age of AI, he added, “people are still the simplest way in.”

Duran warned about the potential damage ahead if we fail to seize this as a moment to change. “If you look at the AI CEO vision of the future, it’s massive economic destruction so that a handful of people can become trillionaires,” he said. “No one voted for that. Nobody wants that, and we have a short window of time to collapse it before they collapse us.”

Disclosure: Katie Collins traveled to Lisbon as a guest of Web Summit to serve as a panel moderator. Her reporting from the event was independent of that role.

title: Nintendo will soon discontinue Google and Apple sign-ins
snippet: Nintendo Switch users have until January 25 to change how they sign in to the Nintendo Switch app on their smartphones. more…
fullText:
Nintendo Switch users have until January 25 to change how they sign in to the Nintendo Switch app on their smartphones.

Nintendo is going all-in on passkeys in a scheduled update to the Nintendo Switch app and will be sunsetting 3rd party logins after January 25, 2027. The news was made available on an official Nintendo support page. That means you won’t be able to use your Google or Apple accounts to log in to your Nintendo account as of January 26. After January 26:

You cannot use your Google or Apple accounts to log in to your Nintendo Account.

You cannot create a new Nintendo Account using a Google or Apple account.

The My Nintendo Platinum Points mission to link your Google account to your Nintendo Account is also discontinued.

title: This tiny iOS 27 camera feature really makes a huge difference
snippet: When shooting both photos and videos on my iPhone, I make regular use of a few different third-party apps, mostly because I like to take manual control. But a combination of the new Pro controls on the iPhone 18 Pro and a new feature introduced with iOS 27 means there are more times when I can stick to Apple’s stock Camera app. If you aren’t already using customizable controls, I highly recommend doing so … more…
fullText:
When shooting both photos and videos on my iPhone, I make regular use of a few different third-party apps, mostly because I like to take manual control.

But a combination of the new Pro controls on the iPhone 18 Pro and a new feature introduced with iOS 27 means there are more times when I can stick to Apple’s stock Camera app. If you aren’t already using customizable controls, I highly recommend doing so …

Developers know that a big reason for using third-party camera apps is being able to use them in much the same way you would a standalone camera. A key part of this is having easy access to manual control over things like aperture (on the iPhone 18 Pro), shutter speed, white balance, and choosing between manual and auto focus. Those settings are right there on the main screen of almost all third-party apps.

With the iPhone 18 Pro, the same set of controls are also available in Apple’s stock camera app. By default, these are tucked inside a menu, requiring an initial tap to open it. As we noted back in September, however, iOS 27 brings customizable controls to the camera app.

Simply open the menu and tap the Edit button (top-left when holding the phone vertically) and you can add any of the controls to the main screen. This makes them available in a single tap.

For still photography, I have these:

Aperture, shutter speed, and white balance as these are the three main manual controls I use. Exposure compensation, because sometimes the only reason I want to take manual control is to increase or decrease the exposure, and that provides a faster way of doing so (quicker than the alternative drag up/down within the photo, in my experience). Finally, I have one-tap access to the histogram to help in setting exposure.

It’s a similar story in video mode. I again have aperture and white balance along with exposure compensation and the histogram. But here I add instant access to frame-rate and focus modes (as I’m more likely to switch focus mode when shooting video).

Of course, third-party apps still have an important role, but this one change has made a big difference to me when using the stock camera app for both photos and video.

title: Wyze’s new door lock has speedy fingerprint recognition and 12-month battery life
snippet: Wyze is today launching its new “Lever Lock,” a smart lock for your front door that has a year of battery life and fast fingerprint recognition, all for an affordable price tag. more…
fullText:
Wyze is today launching its new “Lever Lock,” a smart lock for your front door that has a year of battery life and fast fingerprint recognition, all for an affordable price tag.

Available starting today, the Wyze Level Lock is not your typical deadbolt smart lock. Rather, this is a smart lock designed for your standard single-bore latch, meaning it’s available for doors that other smart locks aren’t compatible with. You can still have a deadbolt, but you’ll need enough space for both (per Wyze’s guidelines below).

The Lever Lock has a PIN entry and a fingerprint sensor, the latter of which Wyze says recognizes your fingerprint in about half a second. It uses local storage for biometric data and works to improve that data with each successful unlock. 

The PIN has a clever feature (though it’s presented in somewhat poor taste) that lets you input random digits before or after your actual code to prevent onlookers from being able to see your code. There’s also a physical key backup as well as a USB-C input on the outside in the case that the battery dies – Wyze says it lasts about 12 months on a charge using eight AA batteries.

	

The Wyze Lever Lock is available today for $99.98 and shipping immediately.

title: Meta’s Horizon+ looks to become Meta VR+ and include 3D movies
snippet: Meta Horizon+ is rumored to be changing its name to Meta VR+ and may start including movies in addition to games with the subscription price. more…
fullText:
Meta Horizon+ is rumored to be changing its name to Meta VR+ and may start including movies in addition to games with the subscription price.

Meta’s quest (ahem) to distance itself from the Horizon era is in full swing, and the latest rumor says it’s time for the company’s Game Pass-like subscription to change its brand name. VR leaker Nori posted a screenshot on X showing a handful of 3D movies coming to the Meta VR Plus service. Considering there is no such Meta VR Plus service currently, the obvious conclusion is that Meta Horizon+ is being renamed once again.

Meta Horizon+ currently includes over 100 games with its $7.99 per month subscription and is similar to Microsoft’s Xbox Game Pass service in many ways. Unironically, Meta Horizon+ also includes the basic Xbox Game Pass tier with over 50 Xbox games playable via the Game Pass cloud. Meta offers a 3-month trial with every new Meta Quest purchase.

The new Meta VR+ service is purported to include 3D movies as well, although we don’t yet know if this will be included in the regular $7.99 per month rate, or if Meta will be introducing additional content tiers, as services like Netflix, Disney+, Xbox Game Pass, and others do. Based on the screenshot, these will be big-name movies and are likely positioned to enhance the value of the upcoming $1,300 Meta VR Glasses, although all the same content will work on existing Meta Quest 3 units.

	

Meta has been slowly distancing itself from the “Horizon” name ever since the beginning of this year, when its VR division got a big reset. In a February blog post, Samantha Ryan, the VP of Content at Meta’s Reality Labs, spoke about the changes to the company’s strategy, including the loss of most in-house VR gaming studios. Since then, several prominent VR developers from Meta have gone on to create independent studios, including the super-popular Supernatural exercise app.

Meta then decoupled the unpopular Horizon Metaverse from its headsets, moving it to mobile-only, and has been removing the “Horizon” name from just about everything since then. Meta Horizon+ looks to be the latest big change, as the company moves toward “Meta VR” branding, which is clearer and separates its VR division from mobile and smart glasses efforts.

title: watchOS 27.3: Three new features coming soon to Apple Watch
snippet: watchOS 27.3 will launch to all users next month and introduce these three new Apple Watch features. more…
fullText:
watchOS 27.3 will launch to all users next month and introduce these three new Apple Watch features.

#1: Siri AI gains new app actions and languages

Siri AI keeps getting new features and also expanding to more languages. And in watchOS 27.3, the assistant will improve in both categories.

watchOS 27.3 upgrades Siri AI with new app actions across built-in apps like Calendar, Mail, Maps, Messages, Music, Notes, Photos, and Weather. With these capabilities, Siri on your wrist can do more than ever.

There are also four new Siri AI languages supported in watchOS 27.3: Chinese (traditional), Norwegian, Turkish, and Vietnamese.

#2: Live Rewind

For the latest Apple Watch models, watchOS 27.3 adds a new Audio Intelligence feature called Live Rewind. Per Apple’s website:

Live Rewind recalls what was just said in the last 15 seconds by showing a text snippet on your Apple Watch when you double-press the Digital Crown, so you can catch something you missed or are less familiar with. You can ask Siri about the content of the snippet or simply save it to the Siri app.

I’m curious to see how useful this proves in everyday life. When Apple demoed the feature in September, it showed Live Rewind being used at a restaurant when an Apple Watch user missed part of the server’s menu explanation. Asking the server to repeat what they said seems like an easier solution, but perhaps there are other occasions Live Rewind will come in handy.

#3: Siri Recap

It won’t be for everyone, but I’ve been testing watchOS 27.3’s new Siri Recap feature and really love it.

Siri Recap only works on Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4, and it’s off by default. But if you have one of those models and enable the feature, Siri can create automatic logs of what’s happening in your day-to-day life. 

Most of the time, you won’t need to reference any of the recaps and they’ll be automatically deleted after a week. But based on my experience with the feature, Siri Recap definitely comes in handy at times when trying to remember key details from conversations.

title: Google Catches Up to Apple, With Digital Wallet Keys for Your Physical Home Lock
snippet: Google Wallet can unlock Android users’ doors who have compatible smart locks.
fullText:
Android users looking for the most high-tech ways to manage their smart locks at home just got some great news.  On Tuesday, Google announced it will start offering digital keys in Google Wallet built on Aliro, a new smart lock standard. 

When I tested the predictive, futuristic Schlage Sense Pro lock — which uses ultrawideband technology and Apple Home Keys in Apple Wallet — Schlage told me that other brands were adopting Aliro to bring that same seamless usability to more devices, and now the time has come.

The best thing about the lock is that it didn’t require me to tap my phone for an NFC connection or even wave it in the vicinity. The ultrawideband, or UWB tech — think of it like an advanced version of Bluetooth older locks used — sensed a key holder was coming to the door, judged my speed and trajectory based on the signals the lock was getting, and had the door unlocked by the time I reached it, with autolock features locking it back up a minute later.

			

More from CNET

Home keys in Google Wallet, which have already started rolling out to Public Preview users in Google Home, offer users a lot of similar tricks with the right smart locks. That’s handy not only for saving time fumbling for your phone at the door, but also if your hands are full or you’re busy talking to someone. When I tested Schlage’s version, it could sense when I was actually approaching and when I was simply walking by the door, too, so the lock didn’t randomly open.

So far, locks compatible with UWB and the “unlock on approach” feature include not only the Schlage Sense Pro ($394.98) I tested, but also the Aqara u400 ($269.99) and the European brand Nuki Keypad 2 NFC lock ($179), with more on the way. Aliro was only officially released early in 2026, so it will take time for the standard to be broadly adopted by both locks and digital wallets, especially more advanced abilities like these. The good news is that Aliro includes encryption for security, battery-life savings and other benefits, too.

A representative from Google didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment. 

The convenience of digital keys in Google Wallet

Google’s new home keys can unlock physical locks in style.Google Home

The “unlock on approach” feature of Aliro’s standard digital wallet keys is only one of the advantages of this upgrade, so you don’t need a UWB-compatible lock to get the benefits.

According to Google, its own home keys in Google Wallet will offer NFC to tap your phone to unlock the door (no unlocking necessary), let you use the digital key across multiple locks if necessary, and sync your key across compatible devices you use. Other people in the home can add their own home keys to the Wallet, but unlike Apple’s temporary passes, Google says guests and visitors will need to get passcodes instead of digital keys of their own.

What happens if you or someone else loses their phone? In most cases, users can rely on keypad access codes to gain entry instead of the digital wallet. But these UWB locks sometimes forgo a physical key slot entirely: Schlage says its lock doesn’t have a key slot to reduce the risk of lockpicking, but that does limit emergency unlock options.

What you need to get started

Here’s where this new lock technology gets more complicated. Finding a compatible lock is only a part of unlocking all these Wallet key features. 

You’ll also need an NFC-enabled Android phone running Android 9 or later, such as the Google Pixel 10 Pro or Pixel Fold. Then you’ll need a Matter-enabled Google Hub with a Thread Border Router, which is typically a separate Google device, like a Nest Hub Max, Nest Wifi Pro system or Google TV streamer.

With all that, make sure your phone, lock, Google Wallet app and Google Home app are all updated, and you should be prompted to create home keys during your lock setup. This takes only a few seconds, and you can delete them easily, just like you could with a concert ticket or credit card.

		

				

					

						

													

					

					

						

Tyler Lacoma
						

						

							Senior Editor / Home Security and Smart Home						
					

											

								

											Tyler has worked on, lived with and tested all types of smart home and security technology for over a dozen years, explaining the latest features, privacy tricks and top recommendations.
With degrees in business management, literature and technical writing, Tyler takes every opportunity to play with the latest AI technology, push smart devices to their limits and occasionally throw cameras off his roof, all to find the best devices to trust in your life. He always checks with the renters (and pets) in his life to see what smart products can work for everyone, in every living situation. 
Living in beautiful Bend, Oregon, gives Tyler plenty of opportunities to test the latest tech in every kind of weather and temperature.
